findings.evidence: code_key_check is SELECT-only for jade_app, and 'the first tool that mints codes inserts the value for its pepper' (RD1). Take the first production batch (jade-t17). The app has run but never wrote a row. The operator's generator environment holds a pepper that differs from the app's. GN3 step 2 finds no row, inserts the CLI's value and mints every code under the wrong pepper. Mike prints and packs the cards. Only when an adult redeems does the app compare its own value, get a mismatch, and answer 'unavailable' for every code. T6 admits 'Before any batch exists there is nothing to compare', yet Q2(5) justifies the stored value because it 'lets the generator refuse before a card is printed', and brief item 18 asks whether a mismatch is detected before printing. For the first batch of every environment it is not, and that is the batch that matters.
findings.fix: Make the app the source of the key-check row. Grant jade_app INSERT on code_key_check (the single-row primary key bounds it) and have the app insert its own keyCheckValue on first readiness or first redeem when the row is absent. Under APP_ENV staging or production, the generator and codes:product refuse with a new tag (for example CODES_KEY_CHECK_ABSENT, 'start the app once first') when no row exists. Under development and test the tool may still create the row. Add a codes-cli case: with no row under staging, the tool refuses and writes nothing. Update T6, Q2(5) and the jade-lnn.2 note to match.
findings.path: plan section 9 RD1/RD3 step 2, section 10 GN3 step 2, T6, Q2(5)

findings.evidence: Processes A and B start together with the same label and output directory, as T4's test runs them. B's batch INSERT waits on A's uncommitted key. A writes its .partial files, fsyncs and commits. B then gets 23505 and goes to step 8. A's partial files exist and every HMAC matches the now-committed batch, so B 'finishes an interrupted run' and renames them while A is renaming the same files. Depending on timing, B exits 0 and A's rename hits ENOENT after a successful commit, or both exit 0, or B fails reading a file A just renamed. That contradicts T4's 'the second fails with CODES_BATCH_EXISTS' and makes its asserted exit codes 0 and 1 flaky. The same race occurs when an operator reruns while the first run is only slow (for example stalled in fsync). Nothing distinguishes an interrupted run from a live one.
findings.fix: Hold an exclusive per-batch lock for the whole run, from before the batch INSERT until after the final rename and directory fsync. Either a session-level pg_advisory_lock on a hash of (product_id, label) on a dedicated connection, or an O_EXCL lock file in the output directory with the owner's pid, released on exit. Step 8 may run only after taking that lock with no wait. If the lock is held, the outcome is CODES_BATCH_EXISTS (or a distinct CODES_BATCH_IN_PROGRESS) with nothing changed. State this in GN3 and T4, and make T4's test assert it.
findings.path: plan section 10 GN3 steps 3, 7, 8; section 13 T4

findings.evidence: The plan names one Phase 1 test it replaces: the migrations-static case 'creates no table'. Several other Phase 1 tests hard-code a world where 0000_baseline is the only shipped migration, and they fail on jade-o07's own pull request. tests/integration/role-bootstrap.test.ts lines 47 and 135 expect applied to equal ['0000_baseline'], and it runs in pnpm test. In tests/integration/migrate.test.ts lines 134-145, migrationsWith adds '0001_extra.sql', which sorts between 0001_citext and 0002_core_schema. The expected ['0000_baseline','0001_extra'] and {recorded: 2, shipped: 1} then fail, and the second run hits MIGRATION_HISTORY_MISMATCH. tests/infra/stack-up.test.ts:72 expects the ledger to be ['0000_baseline']. tests/infra/compose-up.test.ts:193-210 mounts tests/infra/fixtures/migrations/0001_infra_fixture.sql beside the shipped files and expects ['0000_baseline','0001_infra_fixture']. With 0001_citext and 0002_core_schema present, the second up meets a ledger mismatch, and CI's image job runs pnpm test:infra. These are missed call sites. A subagent would have to rewrite Phase 1 assertions without plan guidance, against the plan's own rule that a replaced check is stated, not quietly weakened.
findings.fix: List these in C21/SC6 as stated replacements that keep each assertion's meaning. Derive expected applied lists and ledgers from readManifest(MIGRATIONS_DIR). Number extra or fixture migrations after the last shipped one, as compat's self-test already does with printf '%04d' (for example rename the infra fixture without a fixed number and copy it in as <next>_infra_fixture.sql), and assert recorded and shipped from the manifest length. Add them to AC4's list.
findings.path: plan section 3 C21, section 6 SC6/SC7, AC4

findings.evidence: tools/ci/clean-clone.sh runs the README setup block, then 'pnpm test', then 'pnpm e2e', and only then starts pnpm dev and curls '/'. SD4 says the script prints 'the seconds from the start of the setup block to the first 200 of pnpm dev and the /readyz answer'. Read literally, the figure includes the whole Phase 2 test suite and both e2e browsers. That covers T1's 50 rounds of 16 parallel adults, 100,000 generation draws, CLI process tests and the code-sheet e2e in Chromium and WebKit. Either AC9's 'at most 300 seconds' fails for a reason unrelated to OB25, or the number does not measure 'fresh clone to a usable local app following the README'.
findings.fix: Define the timed span as the setup block (with pnpm db:seed) plus starting pnpm dev, until the '/' 200 and the /readyz 200 with migrations ok. Either move the dev smoke before pnpm test and pnpm e2e in clean-clone.sh, or time the two segments separately and print their sum, excluding the test runs. Say which in SD4 and AC9.

findings.evidence: 'insert ... their code rows by HMAC, drawing again for any HMAC that already exists' runs inside the batch transaction. A plain INSERT that hits kit_codes' unique code_hmac raises 23505 and aborts the whole transaction, so there is no 'drawing again' without a savepoint or ON CONFLICT. A pre-check SELECT does not cover a concurrent batch. The collision chance is tiny, but the mechanism as written cannot work.
findings.fix: Specify INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (code_hmac) DO NOTHING RETURNING id: a missing row means redraw for that serial. Alternatively, a savepoint per insert.

findings.evidence: After the connection is lost during COMMIT, the tool reconnects and 'look[s] for the batch row: present, continue; absent, delete the partial files'. If the old backend is still finishing the commit, or is still holding the open transaction because it has not yet noticed the dead socket, the new session sees no row and deletes the only files. The commit can then complete, leaving rows nobody can print, the outcome T5 says cannot result from a crash.
findings.fix: Record pg_current_xact_id() before COMMIT. After reconnecting, decide on pg_xact_status(xid): 'committed' means continue, 'aborted' means delete the partial files, and 'in progress' or unknown means CODES_COMMIT_UNKNOWN with the files kept for the rerun.

findings.evidence: SC5 says writeAudit validates subjects with 'a strict zod object whose values are uuids, non-negative integers or booleans', but RD4's code.redeem subject has class_id and display_number 'null without a class'. Read literally, the validator rejects the no-class redemption that T1(a) and code-lifecycle exercise, or the implementer quietly widens it.
findings.fix: State per action which keys are nullable (code.redeem: class_id and display_number uuid|null and int|null), and add an audit-subject.test case that null is refused for every other key.
